mainTopic: The height and width limits of a מבוי, and the Temple-doorway sources behind the מחלוקת about its height
overview: The first משנה of מסכת עירובין says that if a מבוי's entrance is higher than twenty אמות, it must be lowered, but רבי יהודה says this is not needed. An entrance wider than ten אמות must be narrowed, unless it has a צורת הפתח. The גמרא asks why this משנה teaches a fix (תקנתא), while the similar משנה in סוכה just says 'פסולה'. It gives two answers. The first is that סוכה is דאורייתא and מבוי is דרבנן. The second is that סוכה has too many rules to list every fix. רב then explains that the חכמים learned the twenty-אמה limit from the היכל doorway, and רבי יהודה learned his view from the taller אולם doorway. The גמרא ties this to how each side reads the פסוק 'פתח אהל מועד'. It then asks how a פסוק about the משכן can teach about the בית המקדש, and answers that each is called by the other's name. Finally it starts looking for a פסוק where the משכן is called 'מקדש', a search that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A tall alleyway entrance must be lowered
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if a מבוי's entrance is higher than twenty אמות, one must lower it. רבי יהודה says this is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: An alleyway that is higher than twenty cubits must be made lower. רבי יהודה says: it does not need to be.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens the מסכת with a rule about how high the entrance of a מבוי may be, and records that רבי יהודה disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying in a מבוי on שבת is allowed through a beam (קורה) placed across its entrance. The first opinion (תנא קמא) says that above twenty אמות the beam does not work, so it must be brought down. רבי יהודה holds the beam works even higher up.

keyTerms.meaning: An alleyway that courtyards open into, and which opens onto a public area
A cubit, a unit of measure (about 1.5–2 feet)
He must reduce it (lower the height or narrow the width)
It is not necessary

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה says 'an alleyway that is high,' but it means the entrance where the beam (קורה) sits. The walls of the alley themselves are not the issue. The point is that the beam across the entrance must be lower than twenty אמות.

phrases.english: An alleyway that is high
phrases.notes: Refers to the height of the beam over the entrance

phrases.english: above twenty cubits — one must diminish it.
Rabbi Yehuda says: he does not need to.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָבוֹי שֶׁהוּא גָּבוֹהַּ לְמַעְלָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, a מבוי entrance higher than twenty אמות must be lowered. רבי יהודה says this is not required.

steps.title: A wide alleyway entrance must be narrowed unless it has a doorway frame
steps.stepSummary: An entrance wider than ten אמות must be narrowed. If it has a צורת הפתח, it does not need to be narrowed even when it is wider than ten אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: An entrance wider than ten cubits must be made narrower. But if it has the form of a doorway, even though it is wider than ten cubits, it does not need to be narrowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second limit, this time for width, and then gives an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An opening wider than ten אמות looks like a broken gap (פרצה), not an entrance, so the beam alone cannot make it work. A צורת הפתח (two side posts with a beam across the top) gives it the look of a real doorway. With a צורת הפתח, the width no longer matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Wide
The form of a doorway: two upright posts with a crosspiece on top
Even though

steps.whyThisMatters: צורת הפתח is the basic building block of most practical עירובין today.

phrases.english: And one that is wider than ten cubits must be diminished.
But if it has the form of a doorway,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא רָחָב מֵעֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת
phrases.english: even though it is wider than ten cubits
he does not need to diminish it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a width limit after the height limit
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An entrance wider than ten אמות must be narrowed, unless it has a צורת הפתח.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the parallel משנה about a tall סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites the משנה in סוכה: a סוכה higher than twenty אמות is פסולה, and רבי יהודה says it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there (in סוכה): a סוכה that is higher than twenty cubits is invalid, and רבי יהודה says it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a similar משנה from מסכת סוכה. It is setting up a comparison that leads to its question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both משניות use the same twenty-אמה limit, and both have רבי יהודה disagreeing. This shared pattern is what makes the difference in wording stand out.

keyTerms.meaning: The booth used on the holiday of סוכות
Invalid
Declares it valid

phrases.english: GEMARA: We learned there:
A sukka that is high
above twenty cubits is invalid,
and Rabbi Yehuda declares it valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside source to compare with the first ruling of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוכה above twenty אמות is פסולה. רבי יהודה rules it is valid.

steps.title: Why does one משנה say invalid and the other give a fix?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the סוכה משנה says 'invalid' while the מבוי משנה teaches a תקנתא (a way to fix it).
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference? For a סוכה the משנה says 'invalid,' and for a מבוי it teaches how to fix it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the two משניות are worded differently even though their rules are similar, and asks why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on the law itself. The גמרא is asking about style: one משנה states the result (it does not work), and the other gives an instruction (lower it). The גמרא wants a reason behind the choice of wording.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference?
Regarding, in the case of
A fix, a way to repair the problem

phrases.english: What is different regarding a sukka
that it teaches 'invalid,'
while regarding an alleyway it teaches the fix?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא גַּבֵּי סוּכָּה דְּתָנֵי פְּסוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the comparison from step 3 into a question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the two משניות use different wording for the same twenty-אמה limit

steps.title: Torah law gives the result, rabbinic law teaches the fix
steps.stepSummary: Because סוכה is דאורייתא, the משנה states it is פסולה. Because מבוי is דרבנן, the משנה teaches the תקנתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: סוכה is from the Torah, so it teaches 'invalid.' מבוי is rabbinic, so it teaches the fix.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference in wording comes from the different level of each law: Torah law versus rabbinic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוכה is a Torah מצוה, so the key point to state is that the מצוה is not fulfilled: it is פסולה. The ban on carrying in a מבוי is only דרבנן, and the beam is a rabbinic remedy. So the משנה naturally speaks in terms of how to fix the situation.

keyTerms.meaning: From the Torah
From the Rabbis (rabbinic law)

steps.whatToRemember: Same height limit, different wording: סוכה (דאורייתא) is described as פסולה, while מבוי (דרבנן) is described with a fix (תקנתא).

phrases.english: Sukka, which is from the Torah — it teaches 'invalid.'
Alleyway, which is rabbinic — it teaches the fix.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wording follows the level of the law: for a Torah מצוה the משנה states invalidity, and for a rabbinic matter it gives a remedy.

steps.title: A second answer: סוכה has too many rules to list fixes
steps.stepSummary: Even a דאורייתא law could have been taught with a fix. But סוכה has many rules, so the משנה simply says 'פסולה'. מבוי has few rules, so the משנה teaches the fix.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say this: even for Torah laws, the משנה could teach a fix. But סוכה has many rules, so the משנה just says 'invalid.' מבוי does not have many rules, so the משנה teaches the fix.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the question from Step 4: why does the סוכה משנה say 'פסולה' while the מבוי משנה teaches a תקנתא?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer said the difference was דאורייתא versus דרבנן. This answer drops that idea completely. Here the difference is practical: lowering a סוכה is not enough, because it must also meet other rules about its size, walls, and סכך. Listing every fix would take too long. A מבוי needs only the one fix, so the משנה can teach it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you want, say' — introduces a second, alternative answer
Its matters are many (it has many rules)
It states a flat rule (without listing fixes)
A fix, a way to repair the problem

steps.confusionAlert: This second answer does NOT say that סוכה stops being a דאורייתא law. It only says that the type of law is not the reason for the different wording.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for the different wording. (1) סוכה is דאורייתא and מבוי is דרבנן. (2) סוכה has many rules and מבוי has few.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Even for Torah law it could teach a fix.
Rather, sukka, whose rules are many —
it states flatly 'invalid.'
An alleyway, whose rules are not many —
it teaches the fix.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer in Step 5 with a different reason
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the סוכה משנה say 'פסולה' while the מבוי משנה teaches a fix?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סוכה has many rules, so listing fixes would be too long. מבוי has only one, so its fix is taught.

steps.title: Where each side learned the twenty-אמה rule
steps.stepSummary: רב says the חכמים learned the limit from the doorway of the היכל. רבי יהודה learned his view from the doorway of the אולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The חכמים learned this only from the doorway of the היכל. רבי יהודה learned it only from the doorway of the אולם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the מחלוקת in the משנה about a מבוי entrance higher than twenty אמות. רב tells us where each side got its number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use a Temple doorway as the model for what counts as a 'פתח' (entrance). The חכמים use the היכל doorway, which is twenty אמות high, so anything higher is not a real entrance. רבי יהודה uses the אולם doorway, which is taller, so a higher opening still counts as an entrance.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary, the main inner hall of the בית המקדש
The Entrance Hall in front of the היכל
Its doorway
They learned it (derived the rule)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole rest of the discussion. The מחלוקת about a מבוי's height really depends on which Temple doorway defines a 'פתח'.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The Rabbis learned it only
from the doorway of the Sanctuary,
and Rabbi Yehuda learned it only
from the doorway of the Entrance Hall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the source behind the מחלוקת in Step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים' twenty-אמה limit comes from the היכל doorway. רבי יהודה's view comes from the אולם doorway.

steps.title: A משנה giving the size of both doorways
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that the היכל doorway was 20 by 10 אמות, and the אולם doorway was 40 by 20 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: The doorway of the היכל is twenty אמות high and ten אמות wide. The doorway of the אולם is forty אמות high and twenty אמות wide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to back up what רב said. It shows the actual measurements of the two doorways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These numbers explain both views. The היכל doorway is exactly twenty אמות high, which matches the חכמים' limit. The אולם doorway is forty אמות high, so by רבי יהודה's model, an opening above twenty can still be a doorway.

keyTerms.meaning: Its height
Its width

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that the היכל doorway is also ten אמות wide. This matches the rule from Step 2 that a מבוי entrance wider than ten אמות must be narrowed.

phrases.english: As we learned: The doorway of the Sanctuary
is twenty cubits high
and ten cubits wide,
and that of the Entrance Hall is forty cubits high
and twenty cubits wide.

steps.raayaObject: רב's statement that each side learned its view from a different Temple doorway
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה listing the doorway sizes of the היכל and the אולם

steps.title: Both read the same פסוק: the רבנן's reasoning
steps.stepSummary: Both sides explain the פסוק 'ושחטו פתח אהל מועד'. The רבנן hold that the היכל and the אולם have separate levels of holiness, so 'פתח אהל מועד' refers to the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both of them learned from one פסוק: 'And he shall slaughter it at the doorway of the אהל מועד.' The רבנן hold that the holiness of the היכל is separate and the holiness of the אולם is separate. So when the פסוק says 'the doorway of the אהל מועד,' it is talking about the היכל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each side picked a different doorway. It shows they both read the same פסוק, and it starts with the reasoning of the רבנן. רבי יהודה's reasoning comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about the 'doorway of the אהל מועד', and the אהל מועד matches the היכל in the בית המקדש. The רבנן say the אולם has its own, separate holiness, so it is not part of the 'אהל מועד'. That means the model doorway is the היכל's doorway, which is twenty אמות high.

keyTerms.meaning: They explained one and the same פסוק
The doorway of the Tent of Meeting
Holiness, sanctity
Separate, by itself

steps.whyThisMatters: The מחלוקת about a מבוי's height turns out to depend on a question about the בית המקדש: do the היכל and the אולם share one level of holiness or not?

phrases.english: And both of them expounded one verse:
'And he shall slaughter it at the doorway of the Tent of Meeting,'
for the Rabbis hold:
the sanctity of the Sanctuary is separate
and the sanctity of the Entrance Hall is separate.
And when it is written 'the doorway of the Tent of Meeting' —
it is written about the Sanctuary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind Step 7, starting with the רבנן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the היכל and the אולם have separate holiness, 'פתח אהל מועד' means the היכל doorway, which is twenty אמות high.

steps.title: רבי יהודה holds the Sanctuary and Entrance Hall share one holiness
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that היכל and אולם have one level of holiness, so 'פתח אהל מועד' refers to both doorways.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה holds that the היכל and the אולם are one holiness. So when the פסוק says 'פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד', it is talking about both of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the explanation it started in step 9. Now it gives רבי יהודה's side: since היכל and אולם are equally holy, the bigger אולם doorway also counts as a 'פתח'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 the רבנן said the היכל and אולם have separate holiness, so 'פתח אהל מועד' means only the היכל doorway (20 אמות). רבי יהודה says they are one holiness, so the פסוק includes the אולם doorway too. That is why רבי יהודה holds that an opening higher than twenty אמות can still count as a doorway, since the אולם doorway was forty אמות high.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary, the main inner hall of the בית המקדש
The Entrance Hall in front of the היכל
One single level of holiness
The doorway of the Tent of Meeting
On both of them

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds:
The Sanctuary and the Entrance Hall are one holiness.
phrases.notes: Equal holiness, so they are treated as one unit

phrases.english: And when it is written: 'The doorway of the Tent of Meeting' —
it is written about both of them.
phrases.notes: So the larger אולם doorway also counts as a 'doorway'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 9 by giving רבי יהודה's side of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, היכל and אולם have one holiness, so 'פתח אהל מועד' includes the אולם doorway.

steps.title: A second explanation of רבי יהודה's source
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, רבי יהודה also holds that the holiness is separate, but he learns from the phrase 'אל פתח אולם הבית', which calls the אולם opening a 'פתח'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: even רבי יהודה agrees that the holiness of the אולם is separate and the holiness of the היכל is separate. Here, this is רבי יהודה's reason: because it is written, 'to the doorway of the אולם of the House'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different way to explain רבי יהודה. He does not need 'one holiness'. He has a פסוק that directly calls the אולם opening a 'פתח'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10, רבי יהודה's view depended on the idea that היכל and אולם have one holiness. Here the גמרא drops that idea completely: both sides agree the holiness is separate. The whole מחלוקת now depends on how to read the words 'פתח אולם הבית'.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces an alternative explanation
Separate, on its own
This is the reason
To the doorway of the Entrance Hall of the House

steps.confusionAlert: The exact phrase 'אל פתח אולם הבית' does not appear word for word in one פסוק. The גמרא is combining language from פסוקים about the בית המקדש. Don't spend time searching for this exact quote in one place.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
even according to Rabbi Yehuda
the holiness of the Entrance Hall is separate
and the holiness of the Sanctuary is separate.
And here, this is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda —
as it is written: 'To the doorway of the Entrance Hall of the House.'
phrases.notes: The אולם opening is called a 'פתח', so its size counts as a doorway

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces step 10's reason for רבי יהודה with a different source, a direct פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה learns from 'אל פתח אולם הבית' that the אולם opening is a 'פתח', even if the holiness is separate.

steps.title: The רבנן reread the verse as the House that opens into the Entrance Hall
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer that 'פתח אולם הבית' means the doorway of the House (the היכל) that opens into the אולם, so it still points to the היכל doorway.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? If the פסוק had said only 'to the doorway of the אולם', it would be like you said. But since it says 'to the doorway of the אולם of the House', it means: the House that opens into the אולם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how the רבנן deal with רבי יהודה's פסוק. They read the extra word 'הבית' as the key to the phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק said only 'פתח אולם', the רבנן would agree it means the אולם doorway. But the added word 'הבית' (the House) changes the meaning: it is the doorway of the House, meaning the היכל, which opens into the אולם. So the measurement still comes from the היכל doorway (20 אמות), and the רבנן's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: As you said
Now that it is written: introduces the actual wording of the text
The House that opens into the Entrance Hall, meaning the היכל

steps.whatToRemember: Both readings work on the same words. רבי יהודה reads 'פתח אולם' as the doorway of the אולם. The רבנן read 'הבית' as the main subject: the היכל, which opens into the אולם.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: Meaning: how do the רבנן explain this פסוק?

phrases.english: If it had been written 'To the doorway of the Entrance Hall' —
it would be as you said.
Now that it is written 'To the doorway of the Entrance Hall of the House' —
it means the House that opens into the Entrance Hall.
phrases.notes: The House is the היכל, so the measurement is the היכל doorway

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's reading of the פסוק that רבי יהודה used in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading of the פסוק based on an extra word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'פתח אולם הבית' seems to call the אולם opening a doorway, which would support רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'הבית' shows the פסוק means the היכל, which opens into the אולם, so the היכל doorway is still the measure.

steps.title: But that verse was said about the משכן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the whole approach: 'פתח אהל מועד' was written about the משכן, so how can it define the doorways of the בית המקדש?
steps.simpleTranslation: But when this פסוק is written, isn't it written about the משכן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the foundation of the whole discussion. The פסוק 'פתח אהל מועד' speaks about the משכן in the desert, not the היכל and אולם of the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides in steps 9 and 10 used 'פתח אהל מועד' to talk about the היכל and אולם. But 'אהל מועד' is the משכן, the portable Tabernacle, which did not have the doorway sizes of the בית המקדש. So the question is how a פסוק about the משכן can teach measurements from the בית המקדש. The גמרא will answer this next.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so: introduces a challenge
The Tabernacle, the portable sanctuary in the desert

steps.confusionAlert: This קשיא is not against רבי יהודה or the רבנן alone. It challenges the shared basis that both of them used, the פסוק 'פתח אהל מועד'.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer will have to explain how the משכן and the בית המקדש are connected, so that one can teach about the other.

phrases.english: But when this is written,
isn't it written about the Tabernacle?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כִּי כְּתִיב הַאי, בְּמִשְׁכָּן כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source text that both sides used in steps 9 and 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of 'פתח אהל מועד' to define the doorways of the היכל and אולם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק speaks about the משכן, so it should not be able to teach about the structures and sizes of the בית המקדש.

steps.title: The Tabernacle and the Temple share each other's names
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 13: the משכן is called מקדש and the מקדש is called משכן, so a פסוק about one can teach about the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: We find that the Tabernacle is called 'Temple,' and the Temple is called 'Tabernacle.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of how a פסוק written about the משכן can teach us about the בית המקדש. Its answer is that the Torah treats them as the same thing by using each one's name for the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 13 the problem was that 'פתח אהל מועד' describes the משכן in the desert, not the permanent בית המקדש. The answer is that the names are interchangeable, so the laws are linked too. That makes the whole earlier discussion about the doorways of the היכל and the אולם valid again.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found
The portable Tabernacle in the desert
The Temple (the permanent Sanctuary)
That is called

phrases.english: We find that the Tabernacle is called 'Temple,'
and the Temple is called 'Tabernacle.'
phrases.notes: So the laws of one can be learned from the other.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Equating terms: the משכן and the מקדש are interchangeable in the Torah's language, so their laws are linked.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A פסוק about the משכן cannot teach anything about the doorways of the בית המקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the names are interchangeable, the laws of the משכן apply to the מקדש.

steps.title: Proof from the law of peace-offerings slaughtered before the doors are opened
steps.stepSummary: If the משכן and the מקדש were not linked, the ruling of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל would make no sense. He disqualifies שלמים slaughtered in the בית המקדש before the היכל doors are opened, and he learns it from a פסוק about the משכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you do not say so, what about the ruling that רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל? Peace-offerings slaughtered before the doors of the Sanctuary were opened are disqualified. This is because the verse says 'and he shall slaughter it at the doorway of the Tent of Meeting,' meaning when the doors are open and not when they are locked. But that verse was written about the Tabernacle!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof for the answer it just gave. A known law about the בית המקדש is actually learned from a פסוק about the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's rule applies in the בית המקדש, which is the place where the היכל doors are opened each morning. Yet his source is 'פתח אהל מועד', which was written about the משכן. Since everyone accepts this ruling, it must be true that the laws of the משכן carry over to the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say so (a proof formula: 'otherwise, how would you explain…')
Peace-offerings
The doors of the Sanctuary building
Disqualified
Locked or closed

steps.confusionAlert: The line 'וְהָא כִּי כְתִיב הָהִיא, בְּמִשְׁכָּן כְּתִיב!' sounds like a new attack. It is not one. It is the punchline of the proof: 'that verse is about the משכן, and still it is applied to the מקדש, so the two must be linked.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical הלכה: in the בית המקדש, שלמים may only be slaughtered after the היכל doors have been opened.

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: then what about that which Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
Peace-offerings that were slaughtered
before the opening of the doors of the Sanctuary are disqualified,
as it says: 'And he shall slaughter it at the doorway of the Tent of Meeting.'
phrases.notes: The word פתח (doorway) is read as פתוח (open).

phrases.english: This means when they are open,
and not when they are locked.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא כִּי כְתִיב הָהִיא, בְּמִשְׁכָּן כְּתִיב!
phrases.english: But when that verse was written, it was written about the Tabernacle!
phrases.notes: So the law of the משכן is being applied to the מקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 14 with an accepted הלכה.
steps.raayaObject: That the laws of the משכן apply to the בית המקדש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל, based on 'ושחטו פתח אהל מועד'.

steps.title: Conclusion: the Temple and the Tabernacle are interchangeable
steps.stepSummary: Based on the proof, the גמרא concludes that the מקדש is called משכן and the משכן is called מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we must say that we find the Temple called 'Tabernacle' and the Tabernacle called 'Temple.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the conclusion that follows from the proof: the two names, and so their laws, go both ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' here means 'so we are forced to say.' The answer from Step 14 is now firmly established. This sets up the next question, which is where exactly the Torah shows each direction.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather / so we must say

steps.whatToRemember: The משכן and the מקדש are treated as one for הלכה, so פסוקים about the משכן teach laws for the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: Rather, we find the Temple called 'Tabernacle'
and the Tabernacle called 'Temple.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the proof in Step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מקדש and the משכן are called by each other's names, so their laws are shared.

steps.title: Where is the Tabernacle called 'Temple'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that the מקדש is called משכן, citing 'ונתתי משכני בתוככם'. It then asks for the source showing that the משכן is called מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the Temple is called 'Tabernacle,' as it is written: 'And I will place My Tabernacle among you.' But that the Tabernacle is called 'Temple,' where do we learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the conclusion it just reached. One direction has a clear פסוק, so it asks for a פסוק for the other direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ונתתי משכני בתוככם' speaks about the future, after the Jews are settled in ארץ ישראל. So the 'משכן' there must mean the permanent בית המקדש. The opposite claim, that the desert משכן is called 'מקדש', still has no source.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable / granted
From where do we know it?
'And I will place My Tabernacle among you'

phrases.english: Granted, the Temple is called 'Tabernacle,'
as it is written: 'And I will place My Tabernacle among you.'
phrases.notes: This refers to the permanent Temple in the Land.

phrases.english: But that the Tabernacle is called 'Temple,' from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the second half of the conclusion in Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק in which the desert משכן is called 'מקדש'.

steps.title: A suggested source: the קהתים carry the 'Temple'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to suggest a source: the פסוק says the קהתים carried 'the מקדש' and then set up the משכן. This seems to call the desert sanctuary 'מקדש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say we learn it from the verse: 'And the Kehatites, the carriers of the Temple, traveled, and they set up the Tabernacle before they arrived,'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to its question. The word 'אילימא' ('if you say') is a signal that this suggestion is about to be challenged in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the desert, the קהתים carried the holy vessels. The פסוק calls what they carried 'המקדש', which seems to show that the משכן is called מקדש. Because the גמרא opens with 'אילימא', a beginner should expect it to reject this proof right on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will likely be rejected)
The family of Levites descended from קהת, who carried the holy vessels
Carriers of the holy things / the 'Temple'

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final answer. 'אילימא' tells you the גמרא is setting up a suggestion that it will push away next.

phrases.english: If you say it is from what is written:
'And the Kehatites, the carriers of the Temple, traveled,'
'and they set up the Tabernacle before they arrived.'
phrases.notes: The פסוק ends here, and the גמרא keeps working through this proof on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a tentative answer to the question of Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A suggested source: במדבר 10:21, where the קהתים are called 'carriers of the מקדש'. This is presented as an 'אילימא' that the גמרא will challenge.
